items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Mom Baker was one in New York

ctx.x: Seven days, yeah. Yeah, we never stay -- we never stayed over -- we played a week, and that was it. And, of course, the biggest portion of our work was one nighters back in those days, you know. Well, we relished the thought of doing theaters. You know, even if you were tied up all day, at least you were in one place, you know. You weren't jumping all around.

You know, most theaters we played, somewhere on that block or on that street there would be some lady who cooked Mom Baker was one in New York. And they were there was always Mom something, and we all would eat there, and we'd run a tap like eating there, and I remember well that dinner was 50 cents then.

We weren't making a lot of money, then either, you know, but we might have three starches on a meal, you know. Anyway, you wasn't hungry. That was the main thing, you know. And then they had some ladies used to fry chicken, make sweet potato pies and come backstage and sell them, you know, and have a basket and come back there, and guys would buy things from them, you know.
